question: The European Union – and specifically the Mediterranean countries, such as Greece, Spain and Italy – is the leading producer and exporter of olive oil, responsible for around 67 % of global production. The trade agreement between the EU and the US includes the application of tariffs of 15 % also on exports of olive oil to the US.

These tariffs severely affect the competitiveness and sustainability of the European agri-food sector, and come on top of a number of challenges that olive oil producers have to manage, such as the impact of the climate crisis on harvests, production fluctuations and price volatility.

Exempting olive oil would benefit European producers as well as American consumers and their health, given the EU’s high safety standards, thus contributing to healthier diets. At the same time, such an exemption would not be harmful to US producers, as olive oil constitutes an ‘unavailable natural resource’ for the US for reasons of geology or climate1. In light of the above, can the Commission say: 1.
Is it considering submitting a request to exempt olive oil from import duties in the US?
If so, what steps has it taken or will it take in this regard?
On the basis of the Annex on potential tariff adjustments for aligned partners (PTAAP).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.1.2026) The Commission recognises the importance of the olive oil sector for the EU, in particular for Mediterranean Member States such as Greece, Italy and Spain, which together account for a substantial share of global olive oil production and exports.

On 27 July 2025, the EU and the United States (US) reached a deal on tariffs and trade1, later confirmed and developed by the Joint Statement2 of 21 August 2025. This political agreement restores stability and predictability for EU consumers and businesses, including by defining a general tariff ceiling of 15% for most EU exports.

At the same time, the US granted a number of exemptions from additional tariffs for certain strategic products, such as pharmaceuticals or aerospace. The Joint Statement also foresees a process to consider further sectors for targeted exemptions.

In this context, the Commission is consolidating a list of potential products, also on the basis of inputs received from EU stakeholders and Member States, for which it intends to seek exemptions from the US additional tariffs. The importance of olive oil has been highlighted to the Commission. A final decision on which products to propose to the US, and at what moment in time, has not yet been taken.
